title: Re-indexing preserves circuit depth
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables and let $f : \mathrm{Fin}\,m \to \mathrm{Fin}\,m'$ be any map of variable indices. Then re-indexing $c$ along $f$ leaves its depth unchanged: $\mathrm{depth}(\mathrm{reidx}(c, f)) = \mathrm{depth}(c)$.
hypotheses_covered: c is a circuit on m variables
f is a map Fin m → Fin m'
replaced:
For every circuit $c$ on $m$ variables and every $f : \mathrm{Fin}\,m \to \mathrm{Fin}\,m'$,
the re-indexed circuit has the same depth as $c$, i.e. $\mathrm{depth}(\mathrm{reidx}(c, f)) = \mathrm{depth}(c)$.
